```{=html}
<div class="dd-hero">
  <div class="dd-card dd-pitch">
    <p class="dd-kicker">Preserving Prusa printers</p>
    <h1 class="dd-title">Restore, don't replace.</h1>
    <p class="dd-lede">Keep the fleet printing. Restore procedures, firmware builds, profiles and a parts list for the Prusa MK2 and MK3. No cloud, no vendor account.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dd-card">
    <h2 class="dd-kicker">When to buy new</h2>
    <p class="dd-lead">Restore, don't replace is the default, and it has limits.</p>
    <p>If a repair or restoration costs more than a new printer, buy new, unless you are sure of better quality or speed, you are trying to prove a point, or you just love the challenge. Have a reason to spend the money.</p>
    <p class="dd-small">The comparison price is low. Amalgam, the sister project, aims at a whole printer for under $300 AUD.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## The mission

```{=html}
<div class="dd-grid dd-grid-3">
  <div class="dd-card">
    <span class="dd-num">01</span>
    <b>Set and forget</b>
    <p>Give a printer the Prusa feel. That is the whole goal.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dd-card">
    <span class="dd-num">02</span>
    <b>Not speed</b>
    <p>If you need to print faster, get another printer, as cheaply as you can.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dd-card">
    <span class="dd-num">03</span>
    <b>Nothing wasted</b>
    <p>Don't retire a machine that still works because something newer came along.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

The full version, and the reason behind it, is on the [Mission](docs/manifesto.md) page.
:::

::: {.dd-card}
## The honest trade

| Capability | Maintained MK3S | Modern CoreXY |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Best-case quality, slow and tuned | Equal | Equal |
| Quality at 150-300 mm/s | Behind | Ahead |
| Tall, thin parts | Behind | Ahead |
| Repairability | Ahead | Behind |
| Firmware openness | Ahead | Behind |
| Cloud requirement | None | Often yes |

The full table, with notes, is on the [Expectations](docs/expectations.md) page.
:::

## Building from scrap instead?

Amalgam, the sister project, builds a printer from two donors. Drydock keeps the printers you already own alive.

[theamalgam.org](https://theamalgam.org){.dd-btn}
